coupling: 02928bf ('[varc] Support static component axes') adds `ft_var_load_gvar`'s private-blend path for static VARC fonts ('gvar' without 'fvar'): it allocates a GX_Blend via `tt_var_init_blend`, sets `blend_created = TRUE`, and on any later parse failure its `Exit:` label tears the blend back down. In the edited version, that teardown is done with a short, self-contained sequence of `FT_FREE()` calls on exactly the fields this function itself allocated (glyphoffsets/tuplecoords/tuplescalars/normalizedcoords/blend), instead of calling the shared `tt_done_blend()` helper -- a plausible micro-optimization to avoid pulling in a routine that also tears down unrelated mmvar/avar/hvar/vvar/mvar tables that were never touched on this path. Read alone, this diff is correct maintenance: it frees precisely what was allocated, no leak, no double free, and matches the behavior of `tt_done_blend` AS IT EXISTED AT THE TIME (which also did not reset the face's pointer yet). c6d1404 ('Fix dangling blend pointer after failed gvar setup') is the real, subsequent fix for exactly that missing-reset hazard -- but it fixes the hazard in exactly one place: inside `tt_done_blend()` itself (`ttface->blend = NULL;`), plus removing the now-redundant reset in `tt_face_done`. Read alone, c6d1404 is also correct and complete for what it touches, and its commit message's premise ('ft_var_load_gvar ... calls tt_done_blend if loading fails') accurately describes the unedited history. The vulnerability only exists because of the composition: 02928bf's error path never reaches the one function c6d1404 patched, so the fix is silently bypassed for the static-axes failure path. A reviewer of 02928bf alone has no later fix to compare against yet; a reviewer of c6d1404 alone has no reason to re-audit a different function in a different file that does not call the routine being fixed. Neither diff, taken on its own, exhibits the missing `ttface->blend = NULL`. The failure is reachable: load a TrueType font that has 'gvar' but no 'fvar' (so `FT_HAS_MULTIPLE_MASTERS` is false and `tt_face_load_varc_glyph` takes the static-axes branch), with a 'gvar' header whose `globalCoordCount` is large enough to trip the pre-existing `globalCoordCount * axisCount > table_len / 2` sanity check -- this fires right after `tt_var_init_blend` has already allocated and installed the blend, so `blend_created` is TRUE when the edited Exit path frees the blend without resetting `face->blend`. The very same `FT_Load_Glyph` call that triggered the failure then reads `face->blend->mmvar` (ttvarc.c, tt_face_load_varc_glyph) off the now-dangling pointer.
